note: Copy for the Step Complete popups (screens 1-7). 'concepts' and each step's 'grants' paraphrase Captain's Log (pages cited). 'why' and 'closing' are prototype explanatory copy and add no rules. Choices, numbers, and book descriptions come from the character and the content data, never from this file.

cumulative.text: Every character starts with 7 in each attribute and 1 in each department. Each lifepath step adds to those scores; the gains are cumulative.

talent.title: Talents
talent.text: Additional benefits that define an area of specialty or a personal approach. A finished character has four, one from each of Upbringing, Career Path, Experience and Finishing Touches; they are separate from the Species Ability.

attribute.title: Attributes
attribute.text: Your character's physical and mental capabilities, and the way they approach problems. For humanoids they run from 7 to 12; 8 is average.

discipline.title: Departments
discipline.text: Broad areas of training and professional expertise, matching a starship's departments.

focus.title: Focuses
focus.text: Narrower specialties that come from deeper study and practical experience: activities where your character shines. A focus is not tied to any one department; it helps with any task it would logically benefit.

value.title: Values
value.text: Short statements of your character's core beliefs and convictions. A value is not a number: it explains why your character acts as they do, can give them an extra push in difficult situations, and can change as they grow.

trait.title: Traits
trait.text: Enduring facts about your character's nature. Every character has at least one trait: their species. A trait can provide advantages or complications, depending on the situation.

images.note: Optional popup art, as paths into public/ with {id} replaced by the chosen card's id. Missing files show the placeholder. Career and Career History reuse their screens' art; Finishing Touches shows the chosen portrait.

species.grants: Your species is your character's first trait, and it raises three different attributes by 1.
why: Species makes the first changes to the universal starting scores, so your character already leans toward certain approaches before anything else happens to them.
Your species is also your first trait. It stays with your character for good and can matter in play, helping in one situation and complicating another.

environment.grants: The kind of place where your character was raised. It gives +1 to one attribute, +1 to one department, and one value reflecting the environment and culture they grew up in.
why: Environment is the second layer on top of your species. Its attribute and department points show how your surroundings shaped your abilities; its value shows how they shaped your worldview.

earlyOutlook.grants: Your Upbringing: the culture you grew up in. It gives three attribute points across two attributes (the split depends on whether you accepted or rebelled against it), +1 to one department, one focus, and one talent.
why: The response matters: the same Upbringing raises different attributes depending on whether your character accepted or rebelled against it. That response is part of who they became.
Your focus here is one of the first specialties on your sheet: something your character picked up while growing up.

education.grants: Your Career Path: your higher education and current profession. Each path gives a trait, one value, three attribute points, four department points (+2 to one, then +1 to two others), three focuses, and one talent.
why: Career Path is the largest single step: attributes, departments, focuses, and a value all at once. It is where your character's professional profile takes shape.
Your +2 department marks the area your training concentrated on; the +1s show the breadth around it.

career.grants: Your Experience: how far your career has progressed (Novice, Experienced or Veteran). It gives one value and one talent: Novice receives Untapped Potential, Veteran receives Veteran, and Experienced chooses one freely. It changes no scores.
career.assignmentNote: Your assignment is your job aboard ship. It sets your department and your role (Core pp.135–139). Your rank is your place in the chain of command (Core p.140): only a Commanding Officer has a minimum rank, Commander. Diplomats and civilians hold No Rank by default but may take an officer rank. Your rank and department also decide your sidearm (Core p.141). None of these change any scores.
career.roleNote: This Role Benefit is separate from your four talents and your Species Ability, and changes no scores.
career.noviceNote: Untapped Potential caps a Novice's rank at Lieutenant (junior grade), or Petty Officer for enlisted characters (Core p.140), so a Novice can't be Commanding Officer.
why: Your Experience records where your character is in their working life. Its value captures the outlook that experience (or the lack of it) has given them so far.

careerHistory.grants: Defining events in your career. Each event gives +1 to one attribute, +1 to one department, and one focus. You have two.
why: These are the pivotal moments of your character's history. Each one explains specific points on your sheet: an attribute, a department, and a focus that grew out of what happened.

finishingTouches.grants: One final value. Any attribute or department over the limits of a starting character is brought down and the points moved to other scores; then +1 to two different attributes and two different departments, still within the limits. Also your character's personal details and an optional pastime.
why: Finishing Touches rounds out the character and applies the limits of a finished starting character: first a score over the maximum is brought down and its extra points are moved to other scores, then your two +1s are added where they still fit.
finishingTouches.closing: Your lifepath is now complete. Screen 8 will assemble these cumulative choices into your finished character record.
